_doc: Prusament PLA (Prusa Polymers), printed, for analysis: a second maker's figures beside pla (Bambu Lab PLA Basic), so a design can be checked against either or see the spread between makers. Along the layers is the sheet's horizontal (flat) specimen; across them its vertical z-axis one, standing. The strengths are tensile yield strengths. low and high are the sheet's own spread either side.
name: pla-prusament

modulus.rule: Young's modulus along the layers (x-y), the flat specimen, ± 100
modulus.source: Prusament PLA technical data sheet version 1.0, 2018-09-20 (ISO 527-1; specimens printed on an Original Prusa i3 MK3, 0.2 mm layers, 100% infill, 215 °C), https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/1745/6181/files/PRUSA_PLA_TechSheet_ENG.pdf

modulus_z.rule: Young's modulus across the layers (z), the standing specimen, ± 100: the sheet gives it no lower than along them
modulus_z.source: Prusament PLA technical data sheet version 1.0 (ISO 527-1)

strength.rule: Tensile yield strength along the layers (x-y), the flat specimen (59.3 ± 1.9 on its edge), ± 2.4
strength.source: Prusament PLA technical data sheet version 1.0 (ISO 527-1)

strength_z.rule: Tensile yield strength across the layers (z), the standing specimen, ± 4
strength_z.source: Prusament PLA technical data sheet version 1.0 (ISO 527-1)

poisson.rule: Poisson's ratio (Prusa publish none): taken as the kit's pla, an estimate
poisson.source: Typical for PLA, as the kit's pla: Farah, Anderson, Langer (2016), Physical and mechanical properties of PLA

density.source: Prusament PLA technical data sheet version 1.0 (ISO 1183)

softening.rule: Heat deflection temperature, ISO 75 at 0.45 MPa: where a part under a little load starts to creep
softening.source: Prusament PLA technical data sheet version 1.0 (ISO 75)
